text:
maria: Hey team — noticed recurring tail latency spikes in eu-west last night around 23:12 UTC. digging into traces, looks like a host-level heartbeat fanout after warmup that briefly amplifies request handling costs.
ken: Can you share the trace ids or a quick grep of the churn logs?
maria: pasted a short snippet from the agent logs: ```
[2026-03-20T23:12:04Z] host=eu-west-3a host_heartbeat_fanout=312 queued_replies=14
[2026-03-20T23:12:04Z] host=eu-west-3a kv_cache_regen=1 heatup_workers=8
```
ravi: That fanout number (312) is suspiciously high for a single host. we usually see <50 during warmup. could be a stale backpressure signal.
liz: Is this affecting dedicated pools or only shared tenants?
maria: mostly shared tenants hitting a single host (multi-tenant), but we saw one dedicated fallback that got routed while the host was still in fanout. that made a worst-case 200ms tail for a handful of calls.
ken: We have a telemetry gap: host_heartbeat_fanout is an aggregate event emitted by the agent but not correlated to per-tenant throttle metrics. so our alerting doesn't catch the impact until SLI thresholds.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy completed for agent v2.14.3 at 22:50 UTC — no global failures reported.
ravi: Proposal: implement a soft-affinity guardrail at the router that prevents routing high-qps shared traffic to hosts with heartbeat_fanout > 100 for 30s after spike. Also emit a per-tenant inferred_throttle metric so we can detect cross-tenant impact.
liz: Sounds reasonable. what's the cost? reserving headroom or doing slower routing increases overall footprint.
k en: Rough numbers: adding a small safety net (5% reserved burst capacity in each AZ) increases monthly GPU spend by ~2-3% but reduces incident MTTR and compensatory overprovisioning.
maria: Another option: prewarm a tiny dedicated micro-pool for bursty high-priority customers. that keeps noisy warmups off shared hosts. downside is commitment and utilization inefficiency.
ravi: Implementation details: router pseudocode idea: ```
if host.heartbeat_fanout_recent > 100 or host.kv_cache_regen_rate > 0.5:
  route_to = find_host_with(soft_affinity && heartbeat_fanout_recent < 20)
  if not found and tenant.priority < high:
    apply_backoff_or_queue()
```
ken: Need to add an index to the host metrics store for heartbeat_fanout_recent and ensure TTL of 60s. Also expose it in the route decision cache.
liz: Operational checklist: 1) add metric 2) router rule + canary 3) small reserved headroom experiment 4) dashboard showing per-tenant inferred_throttle and host_fanout.
maria: I'll take 1 & 4. ken, can you prototype the router rule as a feature flagged canary? ravi, can you run a cost sensitivity calc for 5% reserved headroom vs a 10-node micro-pool for critical tenants?
ken: Yep, will try a canary in eu-west-3 tomorrow morning.
ravi: I'll run the numbers and simulate historical traces to estimate false-positive routing and utilization hit.
liz: Add a short runbook note for oncall: if spikes show heartbeat_fanout >200, consider emergency soft-quarantine of the host and temporary re-routing.
maria: Agree. also adding a small alert: inferred_throttle_ratio_by_tenant > 0.03 for 5m should page infra-sre.
ops-bot: infra-monitor: alert rule created (in draft) for inferred_throttle_ratio_by_tenant.
ken: Thanks — will post canary results and the rule diff here.
maria: thanks all, we'll keep an eye overnight and sync tomorrow 09:30 PT. :thumbsup:
